summary: This note summarizes the consequences of the Black Death, the devastating pandemic that peaked in Europe between 1347 and 1350. It describes the religious, social, and economic upheavals the epidemic caused and their lasting effects on European history. It also gives the pandemic's demographic toll, both in Europe and worldwide, and how long population recovery took.
one_line: Overview of the religious, social, and economic upheavals and population losses caused by the Black Death pandemic.
key_facts: The Black Death was one of the most devastating pandemics in human history.
The Black Death peaked in Europe between 1347 and 1350.
The Black Death killed 30% to 65% of Europe's population.
The Black Death reduced world population from an estimated 450 million to between 350 and 375 million.
Consequences of the Black Death included a series of religious, social, and economic upheavals.
These upheavals had profound effects on the course of European history.
It took 80 years, and in some areas more than 150 years, for Europe's population to recover.
